title: JD.com expands physical AI in logistics with 3 million robots
slides: Can JD.com's 3 million robots outpace human workers?
These machines now handle warehouse sorting and delivery routes
But they still fail at unpredictable, cluttered environments
Your next delivery may arrive via robot—but with limits
Test one robot task yourself before assuming full autonomy
thread_text:
1. 3 Million Robots?

JD.com's robot fleet now sorts packages and plans delivery routes at scale, cutting human labor in some warehouses by half.

2. The Sorting Shift

These machines handle repetitive tasks flawlessly, but each one still needs a human to handle anything unexpected.

3. Cluttered Chaos

Drop a random object in a robot's path, and it freezes. Real-world messiness still beats every algorithm.

4. Your Robot Delivery

One day a bot may knock on your door, but only if the route is perfectly mapped and nothing goes wrong.

5. Test It Yourself

Give a robot one simple task in a messy room. If it fails, you know the limits of full autonomy.

instagram.caption:
Half the human labor in some JD.com warehouses is now handled by machines.

3 million robots sort packages and plan delivery routes at scale. 🤖

They nail repetitive tasks, but drop something unexpected in their path and they freeze. 📦

If you write about tech or logistics, this is the gap worth covering: automation is real, full autonomy isn't.

Would you trust a robot to deliver to your door if the route hit one unmapped obstacle? 🚪
